_meta.source: O*NET OnLine (onetonline.org) occupation summaries, sponsored by the U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration
_meta.note: Each entry's description and tasks are paraphrased/condensed from the corresponding O*NET-SOC occupation's public 'Summary' and 'Tasks' sections (not verbatim reproduction). Keys are the TRADE_CATEGORIES values from infra/lambda/lib/job-fields.ts. 'other' is deliberately absent -- it has no single mapped SOC code, so generation for that category is unsupported rather than ungrounded.

electrician.title: Electricians
electrician.description: Electricians install, maintain, and repair electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures in homes, businesses, and industrial sites, making sure all work meets relevant electrical codes. They read blueprints or sketches to plan layouts, then run conduit and wiring, and troubleshoot and repair faults in existing systems.
tasks: Read blueprints or sketches to plan wiring layout and meet code requirements
Install conduit, wiring, and cable, and pull wire through walls, ceilings, and floors
Connect wiring to circuit breakers, panels, outlets, switches, and fixtures
Test circuits and components with meters and testing equipment to confirm proper operation
Diagnose electrical malfunctions and repair or replace faulty wiring, switches, or fixtures
Inspect electrical systems for code violations, safety hazards, or worn components
Work from ladders, scaffolds, or lifts to install or service wiring and fixtures
Maintain required electrician licensing and follow local and national electrical codes

plumber.title: Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters
plumber.description: Plumbers assemble, install, and repair pipe systems that carry water, gas, steam, and other liquids in homes and businesses. They read blueprints and codes to plan pipe layout, cut and join pipe and fittings, install fixtures, and test finished systems for leaks.
tasks: Review blueprints and codes to plan pipe layout, routing, and material needs
Measure, cut, thread, or bend pipe to the required lengths and angles
Join pipes and fittings using couplings, solvent, soldering, or welding
Install fixtures and appliances such as sinks, toilets, and water heaters
Test installed piping and fixtures for leaks using pressure or water tests
Locate and repair leaks, clogs, and other plumbing problems
Install shutoff valves and connect piping to supply and drain lines
Maintain and replace worn washers, pipes, and fittings during repairs

carpenter.title: Carpenters
carpenter.description: Carpenters build, install, and repair structures and fixtures made of wood and similar materials, including framing, stairways, doors, windows, and concrete forms. They read blueprints to plan layouts, cut and shape materials, and assemble finished work with hand and power tools.
tasks: Study blueprints or plans to determine layout, dimensions, and materials needed
Measure and mark cutting lines on lumber and other materials
Cut and shape materials to size using saws and other hand or power tools
Assemble and fasten framing, walls, and structures with nails, screws, or adhesive
Install doors, windows, trim, flooring, and other finish carpentry
Build and set forms for poured concrete work
Erect and use scaffolding or ladders to work above ground level
Check work for level, plumb, and square using a level and plumb bob

concrete.title: Cement Masons and Concrete Finishers
concrete.description: Cement masons and concrete finishers pour, spread, level, and smooth concrete for floors, sidewalks, driveways, and other structures using hand and power tools. They set forms, monitor curing conditions, and finish surfaces to a smooth or textured final grade.
tasks: Set and align forms that hold poured concrete to the correct depth and pitch
Spread, level, and smooth concrete using rakes, trowels, screeds, and floats
Monitor weather and temperature conditions that affect how concrete cures
Mold expansion joints and edges with edging and jointing tools
Apply sealing or hardening compounds to finished concrete surfaces
Operate power vibrators to remove air pockets and compact concrete
Patch, smooth, or repair holes and cracks in concrete surfaces
Mix cement, sand, and water to the right consistency for the job

painting.title: Painters, Construction and Maintenance
painting.description: Painters apply paint, stain, and other finishes to walls, buildings, and structures using brushes, rollers, and spray equipment. They prepare surfaces by cleaning, sanding, patching, and priming before finishing, and mix or match colors to the desired result.
tasks: Cover floors, furniture, and fixtures with dropcloths or tape before painting
Prepare surfaces by sanding, scraping, patching holes, and washing away dirt or mildew
Apply primer or sealer to new or bare surfaces before the finish coat
Apply paint, stain, or varnish using brushes, rollers, or spray guns
Fill cracks, holes, and joints with caulk, putty, or filler
Mix and match paint colors to achieve the specified finish
Set up ladders or scaffolding to reach upper walls and ceilings
Clean and maintain brushes, rollers, and spray equipment after use

drywall.title: Drywall and Ceiling Tile Installers
drywall.description: Drywall and ceiling tile installers hang plasterboard and wallboard on walls and ceilings and install the framing and acoustical tile that support it. They measure, cut, and fasten panels to framing, and coordinate with finishers who tape and finish the seams.
tasks: Read blueprints to plan panel layout, framing, and material needs
Measure and mark panels and framing for cuts and fastener locations
Cut drywall panels to size and cut openings for outlets, vents, and fixtures
Fasten wallboard or drywall to framing using screws, nails, or adhesive
Install metal or wood studs and framing to support panels
Hang panels on ceilings and walls, using lifts for overhead work
Trim rough panel edges to keep joints even before finishing
Coordinate with drywall finishers on seam and joint locations

general_labor.title: Construction Laborers
general_labor.description: Construction laborers perform a wide range of physical tasks at job sites, including site prep, digging, material handling, and cleanup, and assist skilled trades such as carpenters, masons, and plasterers. They operate basic tools and equipment and help keep the site safe and organized.
tasks: Clean and prepare job sites to remove hazards before work begins
Load, unload, and move building materials, tools, and equipment around the site
Dig trenches, backfill excavations, and grade earth to specification
Erect and take down scaffolding, barricades, and temporary supports
Mix, pour, and spread concrete, and assist with finishing surfaces
Operate hand tools and small power tools such as saws, drills, and compactors
Assist skilled tradespeople such as carpenters, masons, or plasterers as directed
Control traffic or signal equipment operators around active work zones
